interactions.note: R-07: every Speed is 0. The test needs a non-zero movement budget left over from before the grapple, otherwise the empty budget refuses the move before the Speed rule is ever checked.

interactions.with: Dash / Speed bonuses (SpeedPenalty with a negative value)
interactions.note: 'can't increase': Dash and a +10 ft bonus must both leave 0 ft of movement.
Standing up costs half your Speed, so it is impossible at Speed 0. COND-02 already covers this.
Attacks against either grappler have no Grappled Disadvantage. An attack against a third creature does.
The roll mode and the source list must name Grappled, and the grappler's own attacks must be unaffected.
Only the creature doing the grappling can drag the target. Anyone else trying to drag it is refused cleanly.

interactions.with: creature sizes (Tiny exemption vs the two-sizes gap, R-05)
interactions.note: The Tiny branch only matters for a Tiny or Small grappler. A Medium grappler with a Tiny target falls under the size-gap branch anyway.
The extra costs stack: 10 ft of dragging through Difficult Terrain costs 30 ft.

abuse.reason: Grappled sets Speed to 0, so even a 5 ft step is refused cleanly.

abuse.case: Dashing or stacking a Speed bonus while Speed is 0 and can't increase
Spending movement left over from before a Speed-0 condition started mid-turn
abuse.reason: The goblin still has 30 ft of budget, but Speed 0 stops it moving.

abuse.case: Escaping a Speed-0 condition with a special Speed (climb), using leftover movement (added to the catalogue)
abuse.reason: R-07: Climb Speed is 0 too. The leftover budget means only the zeroed Climb Speed can be what refuses the climb.
Session.execute refuses the move cleanly and the position doesn't change.

abuse.case: Dragging a creature you aren't grappling
Dragging a creature someone else is grappling
Dragging past what your Speed covers once the drag cost is counted
abuse.reason: 20 ft of dragging costs 40 ft, which is more than a 30 ft Speed.

output.summary: All 30 GLOSS.grappled tests in tests/srd/test_glossary.py pass. ruff check and ruff format are clean. The previous attempt failed its checks because its report listed only the 3 new tests, so most clauses looked uncovered; this report lists every test for the unit. Coverage: #1 has 2 positive, 1 negative, 2 boundary and 5 abuse tests (Dash, mid-turn leftover movement, climbing with leftover movement under R-07, and a refused Session move). #2 has 2 positive tests (one through Session), 3 negative tests and a two-grappler boundary test (R-06). #3 has 1 positive, 1 negative and 2 abuse tests (dragging a creature you aren't grappling, or one someone else grapples). #4 has 3 positive tests (including stacking with Difficult Terrain), 1 negative test, 5 boundary tests (exactly two sizes smaller, one size smaller for a Large grappler, Tiny dragged by Tiny under R-05, Tiny dragged by Small, and using the whole Speed exactly) and 1 abuse test (dragging beyond Speed). Every test relies only on accepted rulings (R-05/06/07), so no new rulings are proposed. I made no scenario changes. CMB-06 already asserts there is no Disadvantage against the grappler, and the other gaps Stage B noted are covered here. 'Carry' as opposed to 'drag' is recorded as missing infrastructure.
